Overall explanation, causal chain: In an ungrounded system, a ground fault outside the premises raises the zero-sequence voltage V0 across the whole system. Charging current then flows through the ground capacitance of the in-premises cable and passes through the ZCT. The current is I0 ≈ 3ωC·V0, with C per phase. C is proportional to cable length, so I0 grows with cable length. The nondirectional GR reacts to magnitude only, so it can operate unnecessarily when the cable is long. The statement in (3) says 'short', and that is the error. The explanation's check of the formula and its derivation of the answer are correct.

Per-choice reasons: (1) GR/DGR use is correct, and the note that ZPD is also used is accurate. (2) The sequential sectionalizing description is technically sound. It covers no-voltage opening, time-delayed sequential closing from the source side, closing lockout of the switch on the source side of the faulted section, restoration of the healthy source-side sections, and backfeed to load-side sections through a tie switch. (3) The misstatement is stated clearly: the problem arises with long cables, not short ones. (4) The OVGR/DGR roles are correct: OVGR detects a ground fault from V0 measured by the grounded instrument transformer, and DGR selects the faulted feeder. (5) OCR on each feeder for short-circuit protection is correct. None of these reasons conflicts with the official answer.
